preamble: In Mongolic and some Turkic languages with back/front vowel harmony, the velar stop /ɡ/ is retracted to a uvular [ɢ] in back-vowel words. In Khalkha Mongolian [ɢ] occurs in back-vowel words, and /ɡ/ and /ɢ/ contrast only at the end of back-vowel (−ATR) morphemes; Buryat likewise 'postvelarizes' velar stops in back-harmony words (gar [ɢar̥] 'hand' but ger [gɤr̥] 'house'). In Turkmen, /ɡ, k, l/ have back allophones [ɢ, q, ɫ] in back-vowel words. Most Turkic languages instead have a fricative [ʁ] here, so the stop outcome is regional.

examples.from: байгуулагдах baiguulagdakh 'to be organized' (/ɡ/ in a back-vowel word)
examples.note: Uvular realization in a back-vowel (−ATR) word.
Uvular in a back-vowel word, with the preceding nasal assimilating to [ɴ].
Velar stops are postvelarized to uvular in back-harmony words, but not in front-harmony words such as ger [gɤr̥] 'house'; between back vowels /g/ becomes [ʁ] instead.
/ɡ/ is realized as uvular [ɢ] in back-vowel words; it spirantizes to [ʁ] intervocalically and next to obstruents.
